Divergence analysis: B_s2 against A_s2

200 games (100 fresh analysis kingdoms, both seats), 24178 decisions of B; divergence = B's arg-max differs from A's on the same position. Help or hurt: exact values on the held-out bank (1000 buy positions, both seeds).

98/200games B lost
3329divergences from A
13.8%of B's decisions
+0.26bank gain per difference (points)

Key findings

  1. B and A disagree on 16% of decisions (3,329 of 20,849 in 200 games): after the same 100 PPO iterations from starts that differed in 7% of buys, the two branches have drifted apart well beyond the supervised change.
  2. Disagreements are where B is nearly indifferent. B's margin between its top two options is the only signal with information beyond the inputs (AUC 0.60, partial r 0.16; all inputs together 0.595; the random-noise control sits at 0.50 and 0.00). Coin-flip decisions differ; confident ones do not.
  3. They lean to the late game and to buys: 57% of divergences come after turn 12 (42% of decisions), 27% are buys (21% of decisions), 40% action decisions (44%). In 44% of them B keeps c2's choice and A moved away.
  4. On exact values the differences are a wash. On the held-out bank, where B's and A's buys differ (431 positions over both seeds), B's buy is worth +0.26 points of win chance on average; it is clearly better in 18.8% and clearly worse in 15.8%. By phase: opening −0.05, middle +0.61, late +0.13 points. By opponent and kingdom card the groups are small and the sign changes; no card stands out with confidence.
  5. So the verified labels did not leave a lasting, targeted advantage. This matches the promotion match: B_s2 49.9% vs frozen c2, A_s2 51.4%; head to head B led by 3.8 points on one seed and 1.2 on the other.
Proposed next step: If this is tried again
The supervised step moved held-out decisions little (5% of verified pairs) and PPO then washed most of it out. A second attempt would need many more verified lessons (tens of thousands: 20,000 labels gave 389), or a continuing signal during PPO (search-improved targets every iteration) rather than a one-off nudge.

Divergences and results

Games split into quarters by the number of B's divergences. A rising bar would mean B's differences cost games; but long games have more decisions, so read it together with the turn signal.

Findings are leads, not results: validate by implementing the change, retraining, and a paired comparison on held-out data with bootstrap confidence intervals. Numbers in this page come from summary.json next to it.
